rationale: Provider wire serialization, credential rotation and response classification exercise the real APNs client at its transport boundary.

cases.title: signs an ES256 provider token and caches it until the rotation point

cases.title: sends the specified headers, path, and alert body
cases.reason: Inspects an actual client-produced APNs request including alert content, expiry and identity fields.

cases.title: targets the sandbox host and keeps the individual collapse id
cases.reason: Exercises sandbox host selection separately from the production host case.

cases.title: classifies %i %s as a dead token
cases.reason: Covers both HTTP status and provider-reason dead-token branches with parameterized responses.

cases.title: treats %i %s with the appropriate retry policy
cases.reason: Covers permanent versus retryable errors across provider status classes.

cases.title: reports a transport failure as an error rather than throwing
cases.reason: Exercises a throwing transport and verifies the client returns a retryable outcome.

cases.title: does not collapse background dismissals with visible alerts
cases.reason: Verifies a dismissal produces background headers and no alert collapse identity.

cases.title: keeps the absolute deadline across retries and refuses expired delivery
cases.reason: Advances the injected clock across retries and expiry while checking no extra send occurs.

rationale: Protects the real HTTP/2 session cache from a late close/error emitted by an obsolete session.

cases.title: keeps the replacement cached when the draining session closes later
cases.reason: A transport boundary fake emits stale close/error events after replacement; request and close counts prove the replacement remains usable.

rationale: Exercises real stream event settlement and timeout behavior with a deterministic emitter.

cases.title: resolves with the status and the concatenated body
cases.reason: Verifies request-body submission, numeric status conversion and concatenation across data chunks.

cases.title: rejects when the peer resets the stream without an end or an error
cases.reason: A close-only peer reset must reject instead of leaving the request pending.

cases.title: keeps the resolved response when close follows a completed end
cases.reason: End followed by close must retain the completed response.

cases.title: keeps the original error when close follows a stream error
cases.reason: Error followed by close must retain the original failure.

cases.title: destroys the stream on timeout and surfaces the timeout error
cases.reason: Invokes the registered timeout callback and checks stream destruction plus rejection.

cases.title: reports a missing status header as zero rather than NaN
cases.reason: An absent status header must produce zero, preventing NaN classification.

rationale: Real API/store/worker integration distinguishes a topic configuration error from a dead device token.

cases.title: delivers again after a topic error without re-registering the phone
cases.reason: Two API sends separated by a provider topic failure must reach APNs without re-registering the phone; observability distinguishes the outcomes.

rationale: Retain token-bucket, trust-depth and eviction behavior; remove a second replay of changing spoofed left hops.

cases.title: admits exactly the per-minute allowance and refuses the next request
cases.reason: Crosses the configured allowance exactly, detecting an admission off-by-one.

cases.title: keeps one client ip from spending another one budget
cases.reason: Exhausts one identity and proves another retains its budget.

cases.title: refills over the window rather than resetting on a boundary
cases.reason: A half-window clock advance checks continuous refill instead of a boundary reset.

cases.title: bounds what it remembers when a flood of distinct ips arrives
cases.reason: Distinct attacker identities must not grow tracked memory beyond its cap.

cases.title: evicts the least recently used bucket without scanning the map
cases.reason: Checks LRU victim and retained budgets while guarding against whole-map iteration on admission.

cases.title: answers 429 with a rate_limited body once the bucket is empty
cases.reason: Exercises middleware HTTP status and error-body mapping after budget exhaustion.

cases.title: buckets on the last forwarded hop, the only one the platform appended
cases.reason: Changes the spoofable left hop repeatedly, then tests same-client denial and another-client admission.

cases.title: gives a spoofed left-most hop no escape from the caller own bucket
cases.reason: Repeats the preceding middleware case's changing left-hop and fixed trusted right-hop scenario without an additional production branch.

cases.title: skips the configured trusted proxies when counting from the right
cases.reason: Configured proxy depth must select the client before the appended trusted proxy.

cases.title: trusts nothing when the header is shorter than the configured depth
cases.reason: A header shorter than configured trust depth must fall into the shared unknown-client budget.

cases.title: ignores spoofable x-real-ip and uses a single shared bucket
cases.reason: Changing x-real-ip without a trusted forwarded header must not evade the shared budget.

rationale: Configuration parsing tests cover deployment defaults and input validation rather than copying exports.

cases.title: applies the documented defaults
cases.reason: A minimal deployment input must yield operational defaults, including an explicit FCM project.

cases.title: reads a full APNs credential and the overridable knobs
cases.reason: Overrides and a generated APNs key must reach the parsed runtime configuration.

cases.title: requires an explicit FCM project instead of silently targeting production
cases.reason: Missing or blank FCM project must fail to prevent accidental production routing.

cases.title: refuses a partial APNs credential
cases.reason: Partial credentials and malformed key text must fail during startup parsing.

cases.title: requires a canonical HTTPS origin outside loopback
cases.reason: Rejects path-bearing or insecure public origins while allowing loopback development.

cases.title: treats an empty optional variable as unset
cases.reason: Empty optional environment values must resolve as unset.

cases.title: treats blank defaulted environment settings as absent
cases.reason: Whitespace-only defaulted values must match the minimal deployment configuration.

rationale: The independently implemented peer fixture is a deliberate wire-compatibility oracle, backed by a shared fixed transcript vector and live gateway challenge.

cases.title: the checked-in vector answers to the same proof the fixture host computes
cases.reason: The checked-in cross-workspace vector checks fingerprint and transcript HMAC compatibility independently of random live challenges.

cases.title: a live challenge from the store round-trips through the fixture host once
cases.reason: A live gateway-issued encrypted challenge must verify once and reject replay; this exercises the producer against a separate peer implementation.

rationale: Real PostgreSQL transaction interleaving checks a device deletion/registration race that in-memory serialization cannot model.

cases.title: serializes deletion with a registration that has already read its row
cases.reason: Pauses an actual registration read, observes the competing deletion blocked on a database lock, and verifies ordering after release; preserves the DB-only gate.

rationale: Real SQLite queries protect ownership, identity, rotation, revival and quota semantics; API tests additionally cover route wiring.

cases.title: keeps one registration per host and device while replacing the token
cases.reason: Re-registration must preserve registration identity while storing the new token and environment.

cases.title: revives a registration that a re-registered token replaces
cases.reason: A provider-dead registration must become live after the host rotates its token.

cases.title: lets only the owning host delete a registration
cases.reason: A foreign owner must not delete a row; the owner must successfully delete it.

cases.title: scopes lookups and listings to the owning host
cases.reason: Mixed owned/foreign lookup inputs and listings must remain scoped to the caller.

cases.title: refuses a new device once the host reaches its registration cap
cases.reason: The next new identity beyond the host quota must be rejected without insertion.

cases.title: still lets a capped host re-register a device it already owns
cases.reason: A full host must still update a device already registered.

cases.title: frees a slot when a registration is deleted
cases.reason: Deleting a row must release quota for a new identity.

cases.title: counts the cap per host, not across the whole table
cases.reason: Another host must remain able to register after the first host reaches its cap.

cases.title: bounds list reads to the host device allowance
cases.reason: Directly seeded oversized data isolates the query result limit from admission limits.

cases.title: separates the same device id registered against two hosts
cases.reason: Identical device IDs owned by different hosts must receive distinct registration IDs.

rationale: Keep the previous revision SQL as an explicit mixed-deployment participant; replace an unproven sleep interleaving with a real advisory-lock observation.

cases.title: keeps a previous-revision claim from re-leasing a delivery this revision leased
cases.reason: Observe the old revision blocked on the new claim's shared advisory lock before releasing its transaction; finally releases both participants even if the observation fails.

cases.title: yields to a previous-revision claim that already holds the claim lock
cases.reason: An older revision holding the exclusive claim lock must make the current implementation yield promptly and preserve the old lease.

rationale: Real queue transactions cover independent pool progress, per-device exclusion, rollback, lease recovery and bounded pruning.

cases.title: leaves completion, renewal, requests and another store independent of queued claims
cases.reason: Holds three real claims while completion, renewal, request queries and another store progress using spare connections.

cases.title: rolls back a failed claim and admits a fourth waiter while the other claims stay held
cases.reason: A transaction failure must roll back the lease and release admission to a waiting claimant.

cases.title: leases exactly one delivery per device across concurrent claimers
cases.reason: Concurrent stores must lease only the head delivery for one device.

cases.title: does not lease the row behind a head another claimer holds
cases.reason: A locked device head must prevent leasing a later row for that same device.

cases.title: claims another device while one claim transaction is still open
cases.reason: A held claim for one device must not block another device.

cases.title: keeps a device exclusive when an earlier-sorting row lands mid-claim
cases.reason: Inserts an earlier-sorting row during a claim to check device exclusivity under clock skew.

cases.title: never scans rows due before the notification TTL window
cases.reason: Directly seeds stale due rows and observes actual scan results to protect bounded backlog work.

cases.title: keeps claim, exclusion and prune correct without the queue index
cases.reason: Removing the optional queue index must preserve exclusion, ordering and prune semantics.

cases.title: deletes a batch once it is finished, and keeps it only for a retry
cases.reason: Finishing removes a row; a valid retry retains it, and an out-of-lifetime retry removes it.

cases.title: frees a device held by a crashed worker once its lease lapses
cases.reason: A crashed worker's lease must fence other claims until its deadline, then permit recovery.

cases.title: prunes a large backlog in bounded calls without touching live or leased work
cases.reason: A large real database backlog must drain within per-call batch budgets without deleting leased or live work.

rationale: Fixture correctness affects every PostgreSQL concurrency suite; this executes actual scoped advisory locks across two isolated schemas.

cases.title: claims the same device in another schema while a fixture holds its device lock
cases.reason: Checks distinct schemas in the same database, then holds one device lock and proves only that fixture is blocked.

rationale: Remove copied SQL sequence/arguments and repeated derived hashes; retain real stored payload fidelity, one-parse work bounds, fresh objects, rejection and rollback.

cases.title: parses each leased row once with exact complete payload, serialized key order and SQL sequence
cases.reason: Keep exact delivery structure, serialized unknown fields/Unicode and one JSON parse; remove complete production SQL snapshot, redundant hashes and buildPushDelivery compared with itself.

cases.title: keeps concurrent device claims separate and returns fresh payload objects
cases.reason: Two device deliveries must contain distinct parsed objects and parse their respective stored payloads once.

cases.title: reads changed retry bytes and a later writer update without carrying a parsed result across calls
cases.reason: Keep exact serialized retry/later-writer bytes and fresh object checks; remove hashes already implied by the byte equality assertions.

cases.title: keeps dismissed alerts on the original single-parse delete path without leasing
cases.reason: Keep dismissal returning no delivery, removing its database row and parsing once; drop exact DELETE/UPDATE statement spelling checks.

cases.title: preserves the existing trust boundary for an object missing notification fields
cases.reason: An object payload lacking notification fields preserves the store's existing trust boundary without schema invention.

cases.title: preserves invalid payload rejection and rolls back the lease for %s
cases.reason: Parameterized malformed/scalar payloads must reject with the correct error and leave the real database row unchanged.

cases.title: preserves the exact database UPDATE error and retries with a fresh payload after rollback
cases.reason: A real SQLite trigger or PostgreSQL constraint forces lease failure; verify the same database error escapes, rollback restores the row and a subsequent claim succeeds.

rationale: Parameterized real database tests cover all three retention tables and PostgreSQL lock skipping, rather than table-name inventories.

cases.title: prunes expired $table rows across batches and preserves the cutoff
cases.reason: Seeds more than one delete batch in every retention table and checks exact cutoff preservation plus idempotent follow-up.

cases.title: skips a locked oldest $table row until its transaction releases it
cases.reason: Locks the oldest expired row in a real transaction and proves pruning skips it until release while preserving the cutoff.

rationale: Real persistence and state transitions cover acceptance, idempotency, quotas, ordering, dismissal and stale lease fencing.

cases.title: counts a logical event once across phones and separates the 300/15min dismissal budget
cases.reason: Counts one event across recipient phones, maintains separate dismissal quota and recovers after the quota window.

cases.title: queues one delivery per event and recovers work across service instances
cases.reason: A second service instance must resume deduplicated work while stale lease completion cannot erase the reclaimed delivery.

cases.title: never extends expiry and refuses conflicting duplicate content
cases.reason: Conflicting duplicate content must fail and retries must not extend the event lifetime.

cases.title: orders a due retry before a fresh first attempt without delaying the retry
cases.reason: A due retry must precede a new event without waiting for a coalescing interval.

cases.title: orders an expired first-attempt lease by creation time after a retry becomes due
cases.reason: A seeded crashed delivery with a later ordering key must not overtake an already due retry.

cases.title: rolls quota and payload back together if persistence fails
cases.reason: A real missing-table write failure must roll quota and recipient persistence back together.

cases.title: serializes concurrent instances at the quota boundary
cases.reason: Concurrent stores competing for the final quota slot must admit exactly one event.

cases.title: cancels unsent alerts and prevents an older replay after dismissal
cases.reason: A dismissal must cancel unsent alerts and prevent delivery of an older replay to another phone.

cases.title: does not resurrect an in-flight alert after a dismissal and transient provider failure
cases.reason: An in-flight alert retried after dismissal must not be resurrected.

cases.title: normalizes default alert kind (explicit first: %s)
cases.reason: Both explicit/implicit alert insertion orders must deduplicate while conflicting content fails and dismissals remain distinct.

cases.title: fences late renew and finish after an expired claim is dismissed
cases.reason: Late renew/finish calls from an expired dismissed claim must be fenced; subsequent unrelated retry work still completes.

rationale: Retain integration of real durable queue, device registry and dispatcher with fake provider outcomes; scheduler and throughput checks observe actual sends.

cases.title: sends every burst event immediately with its original content and identity
cases.reason: Real stored burst events must become separate provider requests retaining original titles, bodies and identities.

cases.title: keeps untrackable bells and per-phone deliveries individually replaceable
cases.reason: Untrackable bell events and multiple recipient phones must retain individually replaceable collapse identities.

cases.title: preserves provider retry delay when waking a restarted worker
cases.reason: Restarting a worker must honor the persisted provider delay and original expiry.

cases.title: expires instead of shortening a provider delay beyond the delivery lifetime
cases.reason: A retry delay beyond the lifetime must expire work instead of shortening the provider's requested delay.

cases.title: rechecks the device before a persisted retry and does not send after unregistration
cases.reason: Deleting the device before a persisted retry must prevent another provider request and clear queued work.

cases.title: joins active work on shutdown and leaves unclaimed work for the next instance
cases.reason: Shutdown must await an in-flight send, leave unclaimed work durable and release timers; a new worker resumes it.

cases.title: stops queued claim admissions without leasing the remaining device
cases.reason: Stopping while claim admission is queued must not lease a remaining device.

cases.title: claims new devices while an earlier provider response is still pending
cases.reason: A held provider response must not prevent newly enqueued devices being sent.

cases.title: runs due work on its timer and releases the timer on stop
cases.reason: Fake timers verify scheduled work actually sends and stopping clears the poll.

cases.title: wakes only while started and keeps the durability poll
cases.reason: Wakes before start or after stop must not claim work; active wakes send while the durability poll persists.

cases.title: coalesces wakes arriving after every active drain found an empty queue
cases.reason: Holds empty drain responses, enqueues during the gap, and checks coalesced wake processing sends promptly.

cases.title: bounds claims by sends plus drains for a burst and a trickle of wakes
cases.reason: A large real queue burst and idle trickle measure claims relative to completed sends, protecting database workload growth.

cases.title: recovers from a failed automatic wake without leaving another timer
cases.reason: A failing automatic claim must report safely and allow a later wake to deliver without leaking timers.

rationale: Actual provider serialization and response classification are meaningful boundary assertions; no mocked output is being asserted against itself.

cases.title: posts the v1 send payload for the configured project
cases.reason: Client must target the configured project and serialize complete FCM data content, identity and TTL.

cases.title: carries every data value as a string and omits a null agent state
cases.reason: Null state omission, string conversion, collapse identity and absence of auto-display notification data protect Android delivery semantics.

cases.title: marks an unregistered token dead from the status or the error detail
cases.reason: Both top-level status and nested provider detail must classify unregistered tokens as dead.

cases.title: marks an invalid-argument that names the token dead, and others an error
cases.reason: INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the registration token must retire it while a payload error leaves it live.

cases.title: treats a server fault and a transport failure as errors
cases.reason: Server errors and thrown transport failures must yield retryable client outcomes.

cases.title: does not send when credential refresh crosses the absolute expiry
cases.reason: Credential refresh that crosses expiry must suppress the transport call.

cases.title: decreases retry TTL and refuses expired delivery before refreshing credentials
cases.reason: Retries must reduce remaining TTL and expired work must not refresh credentials or send.

rationale: Keep real encrypted challenge, persisted digest, replay, exact expiry and proof checks; remove redundant expiry replay and a negative that validates only the fixture peer.

cases.title: completes a challenge, proof, and consume round trip
cases.reason: A gateway-issued encrypted challenge must carry the expected expiry/fingerprint and verify through an independently implemented peer.

cases.title: never stores material that reproduces the proof
cases.reason: Database rows must store a digest rather than the usable acknowledgement proof.

cases.title: rejects a replayed challenge
cases.reason: A consumed proof must be rejected on replay.

cases.title: rejects a challenge the moment its own ttl elapses
cases.reason: TTL plus one millisecond must reject, protecting the exact no-skew expiry boundary.

cases.title: spends no skew tolerance on its own expiry, so the ttl is the whole window
cases.reason: Repeats the expired branch already checked at TTL plus one, farther into the same skew allowance.

cases.title: accepts a proof that lands just inside the ttl
cases.reason: A proof exactly on the TTL boundary must remain accepted.

cases.title: keeps an expired row long enough to answer expired rather than unknown
cases.reason: Pruning immediately after expiry must retain enough history to return expired instead of unknown.

cases.title: refuses a wrong host: the box will not open and a foreign proof will not match
cases.reason: Wrong-host box opening and foreign acknowledgement must fail, with the latter checked by the production verifier.

cases.title: rejects a proof bound to a different gateway origin
cases.reason: The assertion calls only test-fixture peer rejection for a foreign origin; shipped desktop peer rejection is exercised directly in push-host-proof.test.ts and gateway construction is exercised by live round trips.

cases.title: rejects an unknown challenge id and a malformed public key
cases.reason: Unknown challenge and noncanonical/wrong-width public keys must fail safely.

cases.title: prunes challenges that fell out of the skew window
cases.reason: Challenge pruning must remove rows only after the expiry retention window.

rationale: Real database concurrency checks consume-once across independent host challenges; preserves PostgreSQL execution when configured.

cases.title: accepts independent proofs but consumes each challenge only once under concurrency
cases.reason: Five simultaneous proof submissions for each of two live challenges must produce exactly two successful consumes and eight replay refusals.

rationale: Real persisted sessions cover hashed storage, expiry boundaries, host rotation and pruning.

cases.title: mints a 24 hour session and stores only its hash
cases.reason: A minted session must have expected TTL/entropy, store no raw bearer and resolve to its owner.

cases.title: reports expiry separately from an unknown token
cases.reason: Expired and unknown tokens must produce distinct failure reasons.

cases.title: accepts a session on its final millisecond
cases.reason: The final millisecond is an explicit expiry boundary case.

cases.title: keeps one live session per host and prunes it once expired
cases.reason: A second proof must invalidate the previous host session without harming another host, then pruning removes both expired rows.

rationale: Retains end-to-end authentication/IP budget composition across host identities and routes.

cases.title: bounds valid hosts together across routes without letting key rotation reset the IP budget
cases.reason: Exhausts a shared authenticated-IP allowance across independently authenticated hosts, checks two protected routes, then proves another IP and clock refill work.

rationale: Replace 5ms scheduling sleeps with explicit held-operation gates while retaining actual admission and server-composition measurements.

cases.title: lets background work hold at most poolMax - 1 of %i connections
cases.reason: Hold concurrent queries/transactions at explicit deferred gates until capacity is reached; verify poolMax minus one admission including the single-connection boundary without a wall-clock delay.

cases.title: bounds server claims before they enter the background pool
cases.reason: Observe three actual server claims reach the held database boundary, then release them and verify the peak; removes reliance on 5ms scheduling.

rationale: Fake-clock tests exercise scheduler admission, watchdogs, retry and backlog fairness; store/provider mocks are boundaries, with real DurablePushStore in the fairness case.

cases.title: keeps one slow sweep per store while other stores keep their cadence
cases.reason: A held delivery sweep must not overlap itself or block other cadence; stopping prevents later work.

cases.title: reports a sweep that is still running a full interval after it started
cases.reason: A held sweep must generate a single overdue warning at the watchdog boundary.

cases.title: releases a failed sweep so the next scheduled sweep can recover
cases.reason: A failed sweep must report safely and release its schedule for recovery.

cases.title: resumes a saturated sweep at once rather than waiting out the interval
cases.reason: Saturated bounded sweeps must resume immediately until the backlog drains, then return to interval cadence.

cases.title: keeps a delivery claim behind one statement while a backlog drains back to back
cases.reason: The real pruning loop under a simulated slow SQL boundary must permit a delivery claim behind at most one delete statement.

cases.title: keeps validation mode free of sweeps and timers
cases.reason: Validation mode must not start pruning or timers even after many intervals.

rationale: Mocking pg at its external constructor/query boundary protects URL parsing, pool isolation and transaction retry ordering.

cases.title: passes the Terraform socket URL unchanged to both active pools
cases.reason: Active pools must receive an encoded Cloud SQL socket URL unchanged, preserving credential and socket parsing by pg.

cases.title: parses socket credentials and query options before enforcing validation read-only
cases.reason: Read-only mode must parse socket/query options first and append enforcement after caller options without applying schema writes.

cases.title: applies the schema on an untimed pool that is gone before the serving pool opens
cases.reason: Schema DDL must use an untimed pool closed before serving connections are created; actual schema statements must be applied there.

cases.title: retries a transaction the pool statement_timeout aborted
cases.reason: A statement-timeout abort must roll back/retry the whole transaction and return the later result.

rationale: Real device storage and middleware interleavings guard token replacement and graceful request drain.

cases.title: does not retire a refreshed token after the old token fails
cases.reason: Hold a provider response across token refresh; the stale dead-token outcome must not retire the replacement token.

cases.title: rejects new requests during drain and waits for an admitted handler
cases.reason: An admitted handler must delay drain completion while a later request is refused, then completion releases the drain.

rationale: Production serializers must prevent a dismissal from displaying or sounding like a new alert on either mobile platform.

cases.title: dismissal provider payloads cannot display a new alert or play a sound
cases.reason: Checks actual APNs background content and FCM data-only dismissal without title/message/sound/collapse fields.

rationale: Preserves a compatibility boundary for old messages and runtime host routing metadata across provider forms.

cases.title: carries the workspace server to APNs and FCM, and accepts older messages without one
cases.reason: Real schema parsing and delivery construction must retain executionHost when present while accepting an older message without it.

cases.title: accepts only runtime execution hosts
cases.reason: Schema must reject local/SSH/empty/delimiter-bearing and oversized execution hosts.

rationale: Cross-provider silent preference is a real product behavior guarded through schema and serializers.

cases.title: carries a silent preference through validation to APNs and Android payloads
cases.reason: A validated silent notification must omit APNs sound and select Android silent channel/data; the default APNs preference remains audible.

rationale: Pane metadata and legacy workspace-only messages need compatible provider conversion.

cases.title: preserves pane identity for both APNs and FCM, and accepts older workspace-only messages
cases.reason: Parses both current and older notification shapes and checks paneKey survives delivery construction and string-data conversion.

rationale: A deferred real readiness query proves single-flight and negative caching instead of asserting mock-provided status alone.

cases.title: shares a slow check and caches failures before retrying
cases.reason: One hundred callers must share one pending query, reuse its failed result within the cache window and issue a fresh query after expiry.

rationale: Real PostgreSQL DDL lock contention verifies queue indexes exist after startup retries rather than merely checking their names in source.

cases.title: creates the queue index after waiting out a writer that holds the table
cases.reason: Drops a live index, holds a conflicting writer lock, boots the actual database wrapper and queries pg_indexes plus retry/defer events.

rationale: Real API/store/worker tests protect repeated deliveries across concurrency and mixed client alert representations.

cases.title: returns queued for concurrent retries without double quota or delivery
cases.reason: Concurrent API retries must share one quota event and delivery; changing epoch must deliver again.

cases.title: accepts default alert kind equivalently through the API (explicit first: %s)
cases.reason: Both explicit-first and implicit-first alert kind clients must deduplicate through API schema transformation, while content conflict returns an error.

rationale: Retain real API authentication/device boundaries; focus a copied response-key list on the sensitive-field leak it exists to prevent.

cases.title: answers health unconditionally and ready from the database
cases.reason: Actual health/readiness routes must be available with a reachable database.

cases.title: reports not ready when the database is unreachable
cases.reason: A throwing external database must leave health available and make readiness fail.

cases.title: completes challenge, session, register, list, delete
cases.reason: Real sign-in, registration, listing and deletion must interoperate through routes and persist the expected effects.

cases.title: refuses a request with no bearer, a bogus bearer, and an expired session
cases.reason: Missing, malformed and expired bearer paths must return appropriate authentication failures.

cases.title: refuses a replayed proof and an unknown challenge
cases.reason: API replay and unknown challenge failures must map to stable wire errors.

cases.title: never returns the host fingerprint on the challenge itself
cases.reason: Replace an unrelated five-key response inventory with a direct absence assertion for the sensitive hostFingerprint field.

cases.title: lets only the owning host delete a registration
cases.reason: Foreign host deletion must return not-found and preserve the owner's row.

cases.title: replaces the token on a re-registration and keeps one registration id
cases.reason: Re-registering through the API must preserve ID while changing the stored token.

cases.title: rejects a malformed registration body
cases.reason: An invalid iOS registration must reach schema rejection and return the expected 400 body.

rationale: Full route wiring for body, authentication, IP and event limits remains valuable beyond individual limiter/store tests.

cases.title: refuses an oversized chunked body that declares no content length
cases.reason: A streamed body without Content-Length must still be capped before schema parsing.

cases.title: still refuses an oversized body that declares a content length
cases.reason: Declared Content-Length must take the same payload cap path.

cases.title: lets a chunked body under the cap through to schema validation
cases.reason: A valid streamed challenge under the cap must reach the handler.

cases.title: caps an authenticated oversized send as well
cases.reason: Body limits must also cover the authenticated send route.

cases.title: rate limits one client ip across both unauthenticated routes
cases.reason: Two unauthenticated routes must share IP budget while unrelated and spoofed hops behave correctly.

cases.title: lets a throttled client back in once the window refills
cases.reason: Route integration must return admission after the injected refill window.

cases.title: limits authenticated hosts independently behind the same IP
cases.reason: Authenticated hosts behind one IP must retain individual host budgets without charging the handshake budget.

cases.title: stops repeated forged bearers after the invalid-auth budget is exhausted
cases.reason: Repeated invalid bearers must exhaust their separate budget without creating sessions or charging handshake state.

cases.title: answers 409 once a host has registered its device allowance
cases.reason: A full device registry must map admission refusal to HTTP 409 and preserve the bounded listing.

cases.title: answers an unexpected route failure with a bare 500 and logs only the name
cases.reason: A real closed-database error must yield a bare 500, redact SQL/table data from logs and increment observability.

cases.title: charges a repeated registration id once and returns one result
cases.reason: Schema deduplication of repeated registration IDs must yield one API result, queue row and event charge.

rationale: Retain real API/queue/provider delivery and failure paths; consolidate the lone-event collapse tag check into the existing FCM send integration.

cases.title: rejects a batch over the registration cap
cases.reason: Too many registration targets must reach API schema rejection.

cases.title: queues a send, delivers it to fcm, and reports a dead token on the next send
cases.reason: Preserve queue, FCM body, dead-token persistence and listing checks; also absorb the lone-event tag assertion from the removed duplicate setup.

cases.title: leaves a live registration alone when the provider reports a transient failure
cases.reason: A transient provider failure must not mark the persisted device dead.

cases.title: reports retries from the durable worker after the provider delay
cases.reason: The durable provider delay must defer retry, then observability must distinguish error, retry and sent outcomes.

cases.title: sends a burst as individual APNs alerts grouped by the host thread
cases.reason: A real API burst must generate three independent APNs requests grouped by thread with distinct collapse identities.

cases.title: sends a lone event through unchanged with its own collapse id
cases.reason: Move its only unique tag-format assertion into the existing FCM delivery case; the complete FCM serializer assertion already excludes coalescedCount.

cases.title: reports an error for a registration the host does not own
cases.reason: Foreign and nonexistent registration targets must return errors without queueing the owner's row.

cases.title: rate limits a host that exhausted its 15-minute allowance
cases.reason: A filled real store quota must map to per-recipient rate_limited API results without another insertion.
